j101.text: Last time, clear glass let most light pass through: transparent. Frosted glass let only some light pass through: translucent. Now, the white wooden door!

j201.text: Lock in first. A little moth is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

j401.text: Round one. A wooden door, painted white. The torch shines on it. How much light will pass through? One, most. Two, only some. Three, none. Show me with your fingers.

j403.text: Two! It is white, and white is bright!

j404.text: Three! Nobody found my robot behind that door!

j501.text: Look closer. Torch on. The front of the door is bright.

j502.text: Now look behind it. No bright spot. No glow. No light passed through.

j503.text: And the robot? It is still behind the door. We cannot see it.

j505.text: Oh! White is only its colour!

j602.text: Some materials do not allow any light to pass through them. These materials are opaque.

j603.text: A rubber mat. A metal tray. Torch on: no light passes through.

j604.text: Rubber, wood and metal are opaque materials. You cannot see objects placed behind opaque materials.

j701.text: Three sheets. The same torch. Look closer.

j702.text: Most light. Only some light. No light.

j703.text: How much light can pass through? That has a name.

j802.text: The transparency of a material refers to how much light can pass through it.

j901.text: Be the light! Shrink down. Quietly.

j902.text: You are light from a lamp, in a flat at night.

j903.text: A wooden door. You stop. You cannot pass through.

j904.text: A frosted window. Only some of you pass through.

j905.text: A clear glass window. Most of you pass through, out into the night!

j1001.text: My notes! One: a metal tray is opaque. Two: this box is plastic, so it is transparent. Three: frosted glass is translucent.

j1002.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

j1004.text: Two! I cannot see clearly into that box.

j1005.text: Two! My lunch looks blurry in there!

j1102.text: A clear plastic box. A bright spot: most light.

j1103.text: The cloudy plastic box. A soft glow: only some light.

j1105.text: Glass and some plastics are transparent. Frosted glass and some plastics are translucent.

j1106.text: Two fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

c1003.text: Most light! Transparent! Only some light! Translucent! No light! Opaque!

j1301.text: Show me your score hand! More than one? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

j1302.text: Did you spot the moth? It was by the corridor lamp! Tell someone at home.

j1401.text: Next time: a supermarket trolley! Which material would you choose to make it? One, glass. Two, metal. Three, fabric. Lock in your answer!

j1402.text: A glass trolley! I could see all my snacks!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
